methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native directly address the technology gap through peer-led learning, signaling grassroots capability building outside traditional metro concentrations—a distributed depth approach if sustained.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU partnering with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for community-wide AI education beyond elite programs, potentially distributing deep capability through Richmond's workforce if implementation reaches beyond university walls.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab targets workplace professionals with structured training, creating a secondary hub of AI capability in Southwest Virginia, but its fee-based professional focus may limit broader distribution across the region's transitioning economy.

signals.title: Northern Virginia students build AI tool to help aspiring entrepreneurs
signals.signal_reading: Northern Virginia students building entrepreneurial AI tools demonstrates deep technical capability emerging from NoVA's educational ecosystem, reinforcing the region's concentration of both skills and innovation infrastructure relative to other Virginia regions.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Richmond's young workforce feeling AI pressure without corresponding access to deep training signals shallow adoption driven by employment anxiety rather than capability development, risking skill gaps even in a secondary metro hub.
